name: Efnisien

attributes.attribute: evil brother of Brân the Blessed and author of the war
hero of Wales who wed Branwen to an Irish king
metal that brought the dead to life

sources: Gantz, Jeffrey, trans. *The Mabinogion*. (New York: Barnes & Noble Books, 1976), 77-79.
Monaghan, Patricia. The Encyclopedia of Celtic Mythology and Folklore. Checkmark Books, 2008.
text: Efnisien is a Welsh hero or god. He is the evil brother of Brân the Blessed. His deeds caused a war between Wales and Ireland. That war fills the second branch of the Mabinogion. When Brân agreed that the Irish king Matholwch would marry their sister Branwen, Efnisien stirred trouble. He maimed the Irish horses. Horses carried a sacred glow and were dear to warriors. The act broke the peace and opened war. Branwen was held a prisoner and shamed. Brân set sail with his armies. He had given the Irish king a magic cauldron. Dead soldiers dipped in it rose whole again. Efnisien leapt into the pot to do good. Only the dead could be renewed, so his living body burst it.

okr.objective: Tell how the brother of Brân the Blessed set a war he later repaid with his life.
key_results: He maimed the horses of the Irish king Matholwch and broke a peace between allies.
The war, the center of the Mabinogion, left Branwen a prisoner and humiliated.
Brân carried a magic cauldron that raised the dead.
Efnisien died by jumping into that pot, which only the dead could survive.
